clue.text: Understands when hugging wife and goes from one extreme to the other …

definitions.text: goes from one extreme to the other

parts.note: to see a point is to understand it

indicators.note: one piece holds the other in its arms, so the wife letter sits within the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone grasps things while embracing their wife, then swings between moods.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 9-across, but each stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank rocking up and down is the image behind swinging between extremes, used as a verb.

clue.text: Australian runners will welcome recent copies

indicators.note: the birds take the other word in, as a host receives a guest

parts.note: emus are flightless Australian birds that run fast
late can mean recent, as in 'the late developments'

explanation.surface: Athletes from Australia greet some newly made reproductions.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to imitate them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Suddenly appear in court after season

indicators.note: the court phrase follows the season in the answer

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
someone up before a judge is in court

explanation.surface: A defendant pops up in the dock once the season has turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that arise abruptly are said to emerge out of nowhere, a phrasal verb of quick appearance.

clue.text: Women dressed in the gear for surviving

indicators.note: dressing arranges things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women put on their kit, ready to endure whatever comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' turns IN THE GEAR into EATHERING, which follows W.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through a storm or crisis intact is to ride it out, the present-participle sense of surviving.

clue.text: Duck drink with lass, ignoring idiot

parts.note: tea is a common drink

indicators.note: leaving something out of account, so the fool is dropped from the girl

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone ducks a cuppa with a girl while snubbing a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' strips ASS from LASS, leaving L.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater duck of the genus Anas, an example of the bird.

clue.text: Soft on guest's entertaining language

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A host goes easy on a visitor's talk while hosting them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother tongue means native language, so the word is a familiar synonym for a language.

clue.text: The legal profession love clear title

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
net means clear, as in profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Lawyers adore a plain honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary rank below a baron and above a knight, so an example of a British title.

clue.text: Feels bitter about lease payments covering empty stable

indicators.note: the payments wrap around the other letters

parts.note: rents are payments under a lease

indicators.note: emptying the word leaves only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tenant grumbles that the rent covers a stable with no horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a building to rent; 'empty' removes its inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence at something and harbour grievance over it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: … abandoned and depressed

definitions.meaning: deserted and empty, like a bleak place

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-across, the person rocking between moods ends up deserted and low.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bleak and deserted of a place, and wretched of a person.

clue.text: Very strange county — mostly a lake

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A county that is nearly all lake would be bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY is a county just south of London; 'mostly' drops its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamlike and bizarre, as in the art movement of Dali, so a synonym of weird.

clue.text: Draw attention to European standard-bearer

parts.note: to flag something is to point it out
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: Highlight a European who carries the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard-bearer' suggests a person; here it is the mast a standard flies from.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast that carries a standard, or banner, punning on the military role.

clue.text: Begin to understand amount exposed

parts.note: a figure is a sum or quantity
a secret that is out has been revealed

explanation.surface: Someone starts to grasp how much has been revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something out or come to comprehend it, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Set off, finding answer during meal

indicators.note: the letter falls within the meal word, as an event within a time

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: A boat departs once a solution turns up over lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a ship or rocket going is to send it off, the verb of starting.

clue.text: Promise of union action

definitions.meaning: a betrothal, the agreement to marry

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a betrothal and a clash between armies.

clue.text: Shift AGM — one vote for a change

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A committee shifts its annual meeting because one ballot calls for change.
explanation.walkthrough: AGM is an annual general meeting; 'for a change' rearranges AGM ONE VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shift is an informal command to hurry up, the same as this idiom.

clue.text: List of workers needing uniform

parts.note: men can mean workers, as in 'the men downed tools'
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A roster of staff who need work clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is a list of dishes, so the answer is a specific kind of list.

clue.text: Religious offices may see mostly prudish discourses

indicators.note: the word is kept except its last letter

parts.note: prim means prudish
orates means gives speeches, a verb like discourses

explanation.surface: Church posts may attract strait-laced sermonising.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices held by a prior, or the houses they run, so these are monastic positions.

clue.text: The girl would look and notice a large amount

parts.note: she'd is short for she would
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: A girl would glance and spot a pile of stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a great deal, a lot.

clue.text: Drink and fresh bait eaten by cat

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go inside the cat

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A beverage and new bait are swallowed by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' turns BAIT into BATI, which 'eaten by' puts in LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual pouring of wine to a god, or humorously any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Old boy with debts accepting five will be clear

indicators.note: the old boy with his debts takes in the numeral between them

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A former pupil with five on top of his debts will be in the clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see and evident, the adjective sense of clear.

clue.text: Dries up, accompanied by the Queen on last of duties

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the final letter

parts.note: with means accompanied by
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A companion of the monarch flags at the end of their duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that wilt and shrivel lose moisture, a verb of drying out.

clue.text: The Irish will welcome a person who succeeds

indicators.note: the words take in a guest, so the answer is held within them

explanation.surface: The Irish embrace a successful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' suggests someone who does well; here it means one who follows another to a title.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inherits, taking over a title or estate after its holder.

clue.text: 13's man perhaps may find good space on second-class travel

indicators.note: in an across clue the later pieces follow, set on the first

parts.note: B denotes second class
to ride is to travel
room means space

explanation.surface: Someone with a commitment finds decent room on a budget journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is ENGAGEMENT in its sense of promise of union; the man at a wedding is this.
explanation.definitionFit: The man getting married, which an engaged man perhaps becomes.

clue.text: Join up forming lines on time

indicators.note: the letters form a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Recruits sign up, falling into lines promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: To join the armed forces, which is to enrol, the military sense of joining up.

clue.text: Nothing genuine about Democrat's trial

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: the genuine word goes round the party letter

parts.note: real means genuine
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: No real honesty surrounds a Democrat's day in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful test of endurance, a sense of trial, not the courtroom one.

clue.text: Drug provided by popular mainly healthy worker

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: hale means healthy
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A medicine supplied by a well-liked, mostly fit employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine breathed in, so an example of a drug.

clue.text: Sisters — one in France in the outskirts of Nimes

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: un is French for one

explanation.surface: A religious order based on the edge of the French city of Nimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Women in a religious order address each other as sister.

clue.text: Bank's retainer?

parts.note: money a bank holds on a customer's behalf, read as something kept by a bank; also a sum paid to retain a purchase

explanation.surface: A query about whom a bank keeps on its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retainer' looks like a servant or fee; here it is what the bank retains.
explanation.definitionFit: Money placed in a bank account, and also a down payment securing a purchase.

clue.text: Rebellion at university on the increase

parts.note: a student in residence is up at university
rising means increasing

explanation.surface: Revolt breaks out on campus as numbers swell.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular revolt against authority, a synonym of rebellion.

clue.text: Inoffensive source of delay in anyone on the move

indicators.note: the letter sits within the rearranged word
moving letters around shuffles them
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A harmless cause of hold-up found in anybody who travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' turns ANYONE into ANOYNE, and D from 'source of delay' goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland and unlikely to provoke, a synonym for harmless or innocuous.
